lines: Makes a patch readable at a glance: colours every port and cable by what it carries, and adds several aids to working with the rack; one in a patch is enough, and it acts on every module
Colours every jack by what it carries: yellow for audio, orange for control voltage, light blue for triggers, green for volt per octave, and Rack's own colour where nothing is established
Colours each cable to match the port it comes from; off by default, because a cable's colour belongs to the patch and is saved with it, where everything else here is only drawn over the rack
Redraws every knob in one style, so a rack of modules from a dozen makers can be read without relearning each one
Moves a pattern along each cable in the direction the signal travels, so which end is the source can be seen without tracing it
Lets a two-finger pinch on the trackpad zoom the rack
Dims everything except the cable under the pointer and the two ports it joins, so one cable can be followed through a crowded patch
Picks a cable up from a jack on a click that does not move, where Rack alone would do nothing; a click that moves lands the cable exactly as a drag does
Draws a ring at each click, for a screen recording where the pointer alone does not show what was pressed
Shows a knob's name and value in large type while it is being turned
Turns on the in-rack help: option-click any jack, knob or title band and a note above the pointer says what that one control is
Note — the help is off when the module is added and the switch on the panel turns it on, because the gesture it claims belongs to every other maker's panel as much as to this one
Note — help takes over the option-click menu of clip-on instruments; the same menu opens from the top of any port's right-click menu
Note — the scroll wheel moves a slider the pointer is over. It is on from the start and there is no switch for it on the panel
Note — the port colours come from a reading of each maker's own text and panels, so a jack whose meaning nobody has established is left in Rack's colour rather than guessed at

Menu — Colour and rule sets — which set of port colours and rules is in force: Default, DreamRack, and any set saved to a file, with Custom colours… opening the chooser where a set of your own is made
Darkens the panels of modules whose makers ship only light artwork; the darkening is in memory only, so removing this module puts every panel back
Darkens every light panel in the rack
Note — the in-rack help is a switch on Clarity, not here: it acts on every module in the rack, which is what Clarity is for
Darkener.notes: The Dark module's right-click menu carries the port census commands, and only when a file in the user directory asks for them; see censusOffered() in Census.hpp. They are development tooling that no reader of this help will ever see, so they get no line.

lines: Test gear for the rack: right-click any port on any module and clip on an instrument — an oscilloscope, a frequency analyser, a meter or a voltage injector — which then appears beside that port
One of the hidden jacks this module patches for itself, so a measured port carries a signal or a driven port receives one; the cable and its plugs are drawn nowhere
Note — nothing on this panel is patched by hand; the module is placed in the rack and everything is done from the right-click menu of the port being measured
Menu — Show diagnostics… — opens a window measuring what this plugin costs on this machine, with each part of it switchable, for watching against Rack's own CPU meter
TestGear.notes: Every one of the 21 jacks sits at the same point on the panel (44.85, 351.85) and none is drawn, so a click there reaches whichever the widget list gives last. They share one line for that reason: no click can distinguish them, and the line says what all of them are.

notes: Menu item names read from the plugin's own source. Clarity's menu is Colour and rule sets alone; TestGear's is Show diagnostics…, which reads Hide diagnostics while the window is open; Dark's census commands appear only behind a file check and get no line. Scroll wheel adjusts sliders is param 7 and has no widget and no menu item, so it can never be clicked: the line for it moved from Menu to Note. Clarity's help switch is param 10, off by default, and the modifier is option on the Mac and Alt elsewhere; the lines say option. NOTE FOR A PERSON: research/help/census/DreamerDevelopment.json is stale — it lists the help switch on Dark and gives Clarity ten params, where the source has eleven with the help switch as Clarity's own. The tags here follow the source. Regenerate the census before the next pass.
